jobs.title: Backend Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About

  • We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

  • We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

  • We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

  • We're solving these hard problems.

  • We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

Engineering

Cardboard is a video editor you can talk to. Behind it are proxy transcodes, parallel exports, GPU analysis, AI generation, and the credits that pay for it all.

We're hiring a Backend Engineer to own those systems as products, measured by how fast they are, how often they fail, and what they cost.

What you'll own

  • Exports, media processing, and generation.

  • Long-running jobs that recover on their own and report honest progress.

  • Credits and usage, charged fairly and never twice.

Who you are

  • You've owned production backend systems while the product kept changing.

  • You think clearly about state, queues, and workers, and you care about cost as much as speed.

  • You're strong in TypeScript, and comfortable in Python.

  • Bonus: deep FFmpeg or codec experience.

How we work

  • You own outcomes, not tickets: decide what to build, ship it, and check it worked.

  • You talk to users and look at the data.

  • You build with AI agents every day, and you're the taste and judgment in the loop.

What success looks like

Within your first six months:

  • Exports and processing are measurably faster and fail less often.

  • You know what each kind of job costs us, and the biggest costs have come down.

What you get

You'd be surrounded by people who are absurdly good at what they do. One started coding at 11 and shipped an app with 6M+ downloads in high school. One got into CS engineering at 14 and has been working on distributed systems for 8+ years. One's an ex-founder who took a company to 1.2M users and $300M+ in transactions. That's the team. We're looking for someone who'll raise the bar on technical craftsmanship and product quality. Apart from that you'd get:

  • Competitive salary and founding-team equity.

  • Unlimited tokens across every AI model. Use whatever you want, as much as you want.

  • A healthy budget for AI tools and any peripherals you need to do your best work.

jobs.title: Founding Designer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About

  • We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

  • We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

  • We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

  • We're solving these hard problems.

  • We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

Design

Video is the most powerful way humans tell stories. It always has been. But creating it today is still painfully hard. Fragmented tools, steep learning curves, and workflows that get in the way of the actual creative work. We're building Cardboard to change that.

As our founding designer, you'll shape not just how the product looks, but how it works. You think product first and push back when something doesn't serve the user, and think through every user flow before a component gets shipped.

In our team, everyone has incredible speed, taste, and care that they put into their work. You'll often see people coming up with micro-interactions nobody asked for and losing sleep over things that feel slightly off by a sheer two pixels. Your job is to accelerate and harness that energy to make sure everything we build feels cohesive and intentional.

You will

  • Own product design end to end: flows, UI, prototypes, and everything in between.

  • Advocate for the user in every room like a PM does.

  • Work closely with founders, engineering, and growth.

  • Build a design system.

  • Make something people love.

Who you are

  • You have taste.

  • You own things end-to-end.

  • You think like a PM. You notice the extra click, the label doing two jobs, the feature that shipped but isn't really done.

  • AI-pilled and restlessly curious. Rive, Spline, Paper, Reve, Claude design, whatever dropped last week, you've already tried it.

  • You're a Figma expert. You love micro-interactions. You've probably built parts of a design system, or at least felt the pain of not having one.

  • Resourceful. When you need an illustrator, motion designer, or freelancer, you find them and direct them well.

  • Bonus: you vibe coded or shipped a side project.

What you get

You'd be surrounded by people who are absurdly good at what they do. One started coding at 11 and shipped an app with 6M+ downloads in high school. One got into CS engineering at 14 and has been working on distributed systems for 8+ years. One's an ex-founder who took a company to 1.2M users and $300M+ in transactions. That's the team. We're looking for someone who'll raise the bar on the creative side the way we have on the technical and business side. Apart from that you'd get:

  • Competitive salary and founding-team equity.

  • Unlimited tokens. Use whatever you want, as much as you want.

  • A healthy budget for tools, monitors, laptop, and anything you need to do your best work.

jobs.title: Founding Design Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About

  • We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

  • We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

  • We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

  • We're solving these hard problems.

  • We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

Design Engineering

Cardboard is a video editor you can talk to. In a product like ours, how things move and respond isn't a finishing touch. It's the product.

We're hiring a Founding Design Engineer to own how Cardboard feels and how people see it: in the product, and on the pages and launches where they first meet us. You design in code and ship it yourself.

What you'll own

  • The feel of the editor: timeline, preview, and the chat with our agent.

  • Motion, shaders, and the visual effects people put in their videos.

  • How people perceive Cardboard: marketing pages, launch moments, and experiments.

  • Interface guidelines for the team and the UI our agents write.

Who you are

  • You've shipped interfaces and launches people talk about.

  • You know easing and timing deeply, and you have opinions about 80ms vs 300ms.

  • You're solid in React, CSS, and WebGL, and you can profile a dropped frame.

  • Bonus: creative tools, or WebGPU.

How we work

  • You own outcomes, not tickets: decide what to build, ship it, and check it worked.

  • You talk to users and look at the data.

  • You build with AI agents every day, and you're the taste and judgment in the loop.

What success looks like

Within your first six months:

  • The editor feels noticeably faster and calmer.

  • Our marketing pages and launches set the bar for how Cardboard looks.

  • The UI our agents write follows guidelines you set.

What you get

You'd be surrounded by people who are absurdly good at what they do. One started coding at 11 and shipped an app with 6M+ downloads in high school. We're hiring a Product Engineer (Fullstack) to own features end to end, then watch people use them and decide what's next.

jobs.title: Senior Applied ML Engineer, Evals & Data
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About

  • We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

  • We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

  • We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

  • We're solving these hard problems.

  • We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

AI Engineering

Cardboard is a video editor you can talk to. Our agent makes real edits on the timeline. When it gets one right, it feels like magic. When it gets one wrong, it costs someone their afternoon.

We're hiring a Senior Applied ML Engineer to own how good the agent is: turn real failures into evals, evals into a bar the team trusts, and that bar into shipped improvements. This isn't research-only, prompt-only, or QA.

What you'll own

  • What "good" means for our agent, and datasets built from real usage.

  • Offline and online evals: automated checks, model graders, and human review.

  • Regression gates, and quality tracked alongside latency and cost.

  • Which models the agent runs on.

Who you are

  • You've shipped an LLM or agent system that real customers used.

  • You've built evals, datasets, or AI quality systems before.

  • You can turn "the agent feels dumb" into a number, then move it.

  • Strong in TypeScript or Python. No PhD needed.

  • Bonus: multimodal AI, video, or fine-tuning.

How we work

  • You own outcomes, not tickets: decide what to build, ship it, and check it worked.

  • You talk to users and look at the data.

  • You build with AI agents every day, and you're the taste and judgment in the loop.

What success looks like

Within your first six months:

  • The team trusts a quality baseline for our main agent workflows.

  • Production failures regularly become eval cases.

  • We can show measurable improvements in key editing workflows.

What you get

You'd be surrounded by people who are absurdly good at what they do. One started coding at 11 and shipped an app with 6M+ downloads in high school. One got into CS engineering at 14 and has been working on distributed systems for 8+ years. One's an ex-founder who took a company to 1.2M users and $300M+ in transactions. That's the team. We're looking for someone who'll raise the bar on how we measure and improve AI quality. Apart from that you'd get:

  • Competitive salary and founding-team equity.

  • Unlimited tokens across every AI model. Use whatever you want, as much as you want.

  • A healthy budget for AI tools and any peripherals you need to do your best work.

jobs.title: Product Engineer (Mobile)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About

  • We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

  • We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

  • We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

  • We're solving these hard problems.

  • We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

Engineering

Cardboard is a video editor you can talk to. It runs in the browser and as a Mac app. Most footage is shot on phones, and we don't have a mobile app yet.

We're hiring a Product Engineer (Mobile) to build v1 from scratch, and to decide what Cardboard on a phone should be. We care more about taste and craft than any one stack. With agents, keeping iOS and Android in step is the easy part. Making something people love using is the hard part.

What you'll own

  • Cardboard on iOS and Android, from architecture to the app stores.

  • Handling real phone footage: 4K, HDR, and huge files.

  • Uploads that survive bad networks and the app going to the background.

Who you are

  • You've shipped mobile apps people use every day, and you sweat how they feel.

  • You're a strong mobile engineer, whether that's Swift, Kotlin, or React Native.

  • You notice when an interaction feels off, and you fix it.

  • Bonus: you've built a camera, photo, or video app.

How we work

  • You own outcomes, not tickets: decide what to build, ship it, and check it worked.

  • You talk to users and look at the data.

  • You build with AI agents every day, and you're the taste and judgment in the loop.
